text:
maria: Heads up — after flipping the CUTLASS FP8 build flag (-DFAST_FP8) in the canary pool we saw a 10-15% tail latency regression for mixed small/large seq workloads. Not steady CPU; looks like a kernel-selection/batching interaction. Anyone else see this?

kevin: Yep I noticed the same on the nv-sm90 nodes. P50 fine, but p95+ jumps. Repro steps?

maria: Small repro: run the convo loadgen with 8 concurrent streams, seqs [32,512], kv_cache enabled. I ran with and without the flag. Profiled traces attached below.

ryan: paste of triton profiler summary I pulled from the canary: 
```
KernelSummary: FP8_CUTLASS_FWD  avg_ms=0.38  p95_ms=1.2  calls=12450
KernelSummary: GENERIC_FWD     avg_ms=0.45  p95_ms=2.8  calls=3120
Batching: avg_batch=3.1  batching_hysteresis_ms=5  effective_batch_dist=[1:38%,2:42%,4+:20%]
KVCache: warm_hits=0.72  cold_misses=0.28
```
Looks like more GENERIC_FWD calls than expected and lots of small effective batches.

jen: interesting — FP8 kernels are faster per-token but are triggering an arch fallback path on some sequence lengths (CUTLASS policy returns GENERIC for <4 tokens?). Also the batcher has a low hysteresis so it frequently emits early small batches when kv cache misses cause serialization.

maria: exact: when a KV miss happens we stall waiting for cache populate, the batcher sometimes yields smaller batch sizes and the kernel selector picks the safe generic kernel for stability. Net effect: more kernel launches and slower p95.

kevin: thoughts on fixes? I have two quick ideas: (1) increase batching hysteresis to tolerate short stalls (e.g., 30ms) so we keep batches larger after KV miss, (2) make kernel selector prefer FP8 cutlass kernel for the first warmup window if HW arch matches and sequence length in a small set. Both are low-risk canaries.

ryan: +1 for hysteresis first. Also we should make the arch prober persist detection results for the pod lifetime instead of reprobing per request; I saw repro messages where prober returns unknown, triggering generic.

perf-bot: perf diff (canary vs baseline): overall tokens/s -3.4%, p95 latency +12%. When hysteresis simulated at 30ms in our offline runner p95 delta reduced to +2.1%.

jen: good signal from perf-bot. Two caveats: (a) increasing hysteresis will add avg latency for truly low-latency single-stream requests, (b) persist prober means we must ensure correctness across heterogeneous GPU pools (detect on init).

maria: action plan: kevin will push a canary that sets batching_hysteresis_ms=30 for one pool, and enables persistent arch probe. ryan will run the mixed seq loadgen and capture triton profiler. jen will instrument kernel selector logs so we can see decision reason (arch/probe/seq_len threshold). I'll also try a KV warmup prefetch on route entry to reduce miss rate.

kevin: canary pushed to canary-pool-3 with flags: `--batching_hysteresis_ms=30 --arch_prober=persist --cutlass_pref=prefer`

ryan: running loadgen now, will drop traces in #eng-runtime once done.

infra-bot: deploy notification: canary-pool-3 updated at 2026-03-18T14:12:10Z by kevin.

maria: thanks. If hysteresis fixes the p95 we can consider defaulting to 20-30ms and add an override for single-stream SLA routes.

jen: note for follow-up: add a metric for "kernel_fallback_rate" (count of GENERIC_FWD decisions when CUTLASS available) and expose per-route. That will help catch regressions earlier.

kevin: noted. I'll add the metric to the canary.

ryan: traces uploaded — initial look shows GENERIC_FWD ratio dropped from 20%->6% in the canary, p95 improved to +1.8% vs baseline. Will do more runs tonight.

maria: great, closing loop in the morning. :thumbsup:
